absent: Numeric page size and address width and byte width that determine KHO radix and vmalloc capacities.
Layout and lifetime of virtual console and key and task and device and module and firmware objects referenced but not defined.
Concurrency and ordering and failure handling for keyboard notifier and message dump list and module loader and live update chains.
Allocation and growth and error paths for vmalloc chunks and radix nodes and bad range entries and region mappings.
Enforcement behavior for Landlock rights and latency collection thresholds and stack erasure scheduling.
Physical to virtual translation guarantees and device tree parsing for handover properties.

findings.text: Keyboard notification delivery uses a small carrier that links the target virtual console with press direction and modifier state plus indicator state and a numeric payload for keycode or character value. The console link is known as vc while the press flag is known as down and the modifier mask is known as shift with indicator snapshot known as ledstate and payload known as value.

Public key capability description reports supported operations plus key length in bits and four size limits for raw data and signature and encrypted blob and decrypted blob. The operation mask is called supported_ops and key length is called key_size while limits are called max_data_size and max_sig_size and max_enc_size and max_dec_size.

Public key operation request bundles a key reference with encoding name and hash name and mutable info string and input length and a dual purpose second length. That second length means output capacity for encrypt decrypt and sign but second input length for verify. Members are called key and encoding and hash_algo and info and in_len with action selector called op.

Public key actions form four distinct modes for encryption and decryption and signing and verification with no intermediate states shown. Callers select one mode per request and the parameter block interprets length fields according to that choice.
Kexec handover block size equals the platform page size.
Preserved block header for serialization holds a link to the next block and a count of entries packed without padding. The link field is called next and the count field is called count.

Kexec handover device tree identifiers use kho-v4 for compatibility and preserved-memory-map for the memory map property and preserved-data for the subtree name and blob-size for the subtree size property.

Serializable pointers are represented as a union of a physical address integer and a typed virtual pointer sharing storage. Storing converts a virtual address to physical after checking type compatibility while loading converts a nonzero physical address back to virtual or yields null when zero. The union members are phys and ptr.

Discontiguous preserved memory uses a header with a serializable link to chunks where each chunk pairs that header with an array of physical page addresses. A top descriptor holds a serializable first link plus total page count and flags and order. Chunk capacity derives from page size minus header size divided by address size. Counts are called total_pages with flags and order.

Preserved page tracking uses a radix tree whose key width and table fanout and bitmap span and maximum depth derive from address width and page size and byte width. Interior nodes hold a table of physical addresses sized as a power of two while leaves hold a bitmap sized as a power of two. Members are called table and bitmap.

Live update handover names the top entry LUO with compatibility luo-v5 aligned to eight bytes. Handle and file backed labels allow forty eight bytes each and test file labels combine a fixed prefix with a version numeral.

Live update serialization is packed and physical address based. The top record carries compatibility text and session count and two physical addresses for sessions and file backed blobs. File records carry compatibility text plus data address and token. File sets carry a files address and count. Sessions carry a name plus embedded file set. Blob headers carry page and entry counts while blob entries carry a name plus data address and count.
Memory block handover uses memblock as the container label and memblock-v1 for node compatibility and reserve-mem-v1 for reserved memory node compatibility.

Memfd live update folio marks use the lowest bit for dirty and the next bit for uptodate. The seal aggregate covers seal and shrink and grow and write and future write and exec variants. The file handle compatibility label is memfd-v2.

Memfd folio serialization packs a page frame number with flag bits plus an index. File serialization is packed and holds file position and size and seal set and flags and folio count and an embedded discontiguous folio list using the kexec handover vmalloc descriptor.

Module loading helpers offer blocking and nonblocking request forms plus a test then request helper that evaluates its first argument and only requests on falsy input. When the loader is unavailable the blocking and nonblocking forms report not implemented and the conditional form simply returns its input.

Kernel message dump triggers progress through undefined and panic and oops and emergency and shutdown and a maximum sentinel that bounds the set. No transitions are defined in the fragments beyond enumeration ordering.

Dump iteration tracks current and next sequence numbers. Dump detail pairs a trigger reason with a descriptive string. Dump handlers link into a list and provide a callback receiving handler and detail with a maximum reason filter and a registration flag.

When dumping is disabled the control helpers become inert shims. Description and rewind do nothing and line and buffer retrieval report failure and registration reports invalid argument and reason text reports disabled. The top level dump entry forwards to description with no string.

Device number probing uses a callback type that receives a device number and a length pointer and opaque data and returns a kernel object. The probe map itself is an opaque incomplete type whose layout is not shown.
Reference counting wraps a single counter. Static initialization sets the counter to a caller supplied start value while dynamic initialization sets it to one.

A fresh reference starts at one and reading returns the current count. Unconditional acquisition increments while conditional acquisition only succeeds when the count is already nonzero. Release on last drop invokes a caller supplied cleanup and reports success otherwise it reports survival without invoking cleanup.

Last drop can atomically acquire an external mutex or spin lock before invoking cleanup with success meaning the lock is held on return. Separately the bad range tracker protects its list with its own spin lock.

Reference helpers provide init and read and unconditional get and conditional get and three put variants for plain and mutex protected and spin protected release. Puts return a small integer distinguishing last drop from remaining references.

Kernel stack erasure uses a negative poison word and a bounded search depth of one hundred twenty eight bytes. The erasable span runs from just above the stack end magic to the saved register area. Scanning moves downward from the top counting consecutive poison words and resetting on first nonpoison returning the highest nonpoison boundary.

Task stack tracking initializes the lowest seen stack marker to the low bound optionally duplicating it as previous low when metrics are enabled or does nothing in the disabled build. Low and high bound helpers expose the erasable limits for other passes.

Landlock display tables pair each numeric right with a short lower case label. Filesystem rights cover execution and file and directory access and removal and node creation and referral and truncation and device control plus unix resolution. Network rights cover bind and connect for datagram and stream transports. Scope rights cover abstract sockets and signaling.
Latency sampling keeps thirty two saved entries each with a twelve deep address trace plus count and total time and maximum time. Depths and capacities are fixed small constants.
Scheduler latency accounting forwards to an underlying collector only when enabled otherwise it does nothing and task tracing state can be cleared through a small inline helper.

Flattened device tree environment aliases signed and unsigned thirty two bit maxima to kernel limits and defines three big endian integer widths with paired conversions between host and device order for thirty two and sixty four bit values.

Compiler support defines a machine word integer and a double word split into high and low halves with two orderings for differing endianness. A union overlays that split view with a single sixty four bit integer.
Bad range tracking links entries each carrying a start address and length. The container holds a list head guarded by a spin lock.

Nonvolatile memory state uses small numeric markers for unarmed and locked and security overwrite and work pending and labeling and incoherence and synchronous registration plus region persistence and async behaviors with a flag for adjusted resources requiring label update.
Nonvolatile memory limits allow four megabytes for ioctl buffers and five command elements and two hundred fifty six bytes of envelope and thirty two mappings per region.

Nonvolatile bus description carries attribute groups and command and family masks and module and provider identity and device tree link and control callback and optional flush probe and gate and firmware operations. Command description gives input and output counts with per element sizes. Interleave description holds three cookies plus a type identifier. Mapping description links a dimm with start and size and position. Region description adds resources and mappings and lane count and nodes and flags and memory region and tree link and flush callback with an async flush marker.
Device managed nonvolatile remapping exposes a small inline that forwards offset and length to an underlying managed mapping primitive with default flags and returns an input output pointer.
Public inline services include reference count management and message dump registration and triggering usable without external linkage in headers.

Releasing the last reference invokes cleanup while holding the supplied lock so cleanup must not reacquire the same lock. Stack poison scanning dereferences raw stack words and assumes low precedes high. Loading a serialized pointer trusts the stored physical address and only guards the zero case. Conditional acquisition can still race to zero immediately after success if callers do not hold another guard.
Each header in this lane defines a single inclusion guard macro that prevents multiple inclusion and carries no runtime behavior.
